title: Compact session prefetch + tool-call circuit breaker (PRD notes)
content:
Context / motivation:

We continue to see two recurring developer problems with hosted streaming + tool integration: (1) spikes in tail latency when a session needs to hydrate tool adapters or cold-start toollets mid-stream, and (2) brittle client behavior in the presence of transient downstream tool failures and network flakiness. Both cause degraded UX (stalls, truncated incremental output, or confusing errors) and higher reattempt cost at the platform level.

Goal (high level):
- Reduce visible stalls for progressive/streaming responses when tool calls are likely to be invoked.
- Give SDKs a small, deterministic surface for graceful degradation: prefetch confidence hints + circuit-breaker signals so clients can choose fidelity fallbacks.
- Ensure server-side cost and complexity tradeoffs are bounded: prefetch must be compact (low memory/IO) and optional per-session.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to replace broader rollout/traffic-splitting systems (canary/A-B).
- Not adding heavyweight per-customer caching tier or persistent tool VM pools in this phase.

User stories / examples:
1) Messaging assistant: user asks to summarize a long thread and call an external search tool to fetch citations. The model will likely call the search tool for specific lines; prefetch should warm the search tool adapter and query plan so the first tool call completes without blocking the stream for >150ms.
2) Form-filling bot on mobile: intermittent mobile connectivity may break a backend tool call (payment API). SDK should surface a circuit-breaker so the UI shows a degraded inline result + a retry affordance instead of crashing the session.
3) Low-bandwidth edge client: prefers compact prefetch to avoid extra bytes but can opt-in to a more aggressive prefetch when on Wi-Fi.

Design overview (proposal):
1) Compact session prefetch metadata (handshake-level): when a session is created, clients may optionally include a prefetch hint blob describing upcoming tool intentions. The hint is intentionally small (~1kB max) and schema-driven: tool_id, expected_call_patterns (e.g., frequency: once|many|unknown), priority: high|normal|low, and an optional short JSONL of minimal seed args. Server uses the hint for two lightweight actions: allocate a hot adapter handle (soft-warm) and prime per-session routing/cache entries (no heavyweight compilation or VM boot).

2) Server semantics: soft-warm adapters are not guaranteed; they are a hint. Admission controlled by a per-region budget and per-customer throttle (configurable in Console). When budget is low, server may evict soft-warm handles; the session receives a lightweight "prefetch.status" event in the incremental stream (see telemetry below) indicating hit/miss.

3) Circuit breaker tokens & SDK contract: the server exposes a small set of tokens in the streaming frame namespace: "tool:cb:open", "tool:cb:warn", "tool:cb:ok". SDKs map these to client-visible states: open -> show degraded UX / offer manual retry; warn -> slow but likely recovering; ok -> full fidelity. Tokens are emitted inline during the incremental stream when the runtime detects downstream error patterns or sustained latency.

4) Fallback policies (server-side): a policy language defines per-tool fallback behaviors (configurable in Console and set by product defaults):
- Fail-soft: return partial text with placeholder and continue streaming.
- Queue-for-retry: buffer a toolcall for a short period (e.g., 500–2000ms) while continuing speculative token streaming.
- Switch-variant: route to a cheaper or more robust tool variant if available (e.g., degrade to cached search index).

5) SDK ergonomics (developer-facing):
- New SDK helper: session.prefetch(hints, options) that serializes the compact hint and negotiates soft-warm. Returns a short status object: ["prefetch_ack": true/false, "expected_warm_ms": "<50|<200|unknown", "session_token"] as part of the call create flow.
- Stream frame handler: SDKs expose onToolCircuit(token, meta) callbacks and a concise state machine so apps can wire UI quickly.
- Fallback templates: small reference components (React + Swift + Kotlin) that map tokens to UI affordances (skeletons, retry buttons, low-fidelity substitute text).

Protocol changes (compact, incremental):
- Add small JSONL event envelope inside the existing incremental frames: {"event":"prefetch.status","status":"hit|miss|throttle","latency_ms":int}.
- Add an optional event: {"event":"tool.circuit","state":"open|warn|ok","reason":"timeout|error|quota", "tool_id":"..."} emitted inline.
- Keep payloads minimal and backward-compatible: clients that ignore unknown event types continue to work.

Observability and metrics:
- Prefetch hit rate (per-tool, per-customer).
- Average stall reduction: measure delta between first-byte-to-first-tool-response for sessions with and without prefetch hints (sampled).
- Circuit-breaker open time, reason breakdown.
- SDK-level telemetry: client-reported fallback (user clicked retry, user accepted degraded output).

Acceptance criteria / KPI:
- 30% reduction in median tool-call tail latency for instrumented sessions in dev-sandbox within 6 weeks of rollout.
- <10% false-positive circuit-breaker opens (i.e., opens where subsequent requests succeed without fallback).
- SDK adoption: reference widgets used by at least two internal apps within 2 months.

Operational controls / console knobs:
- Global soft-warm budget (region-level allocation).
- Per-customer prefetch throttle and disable flag.
- Tool-level fallback policy editor (select default fail-soft/queue/switch-variant).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (lab): internal-only SDK + runtime flag. Run with SearchTool, PaymentTool on staging.
- Phase 1 (beta): opt-in customers and internal apps. Enable prefetch hints by default but conservative budgets. Collect metrics.
- Phase 2 (GA): enable by default with per-customer toggles and alerts on unusual budgets.

Security & privacy notes:
- Prefetch hints must not include PII or sensitive secrets. We will validate and strip keys; Console will show a warning.
- Tool seed args are truncated to 1kB and scanned for obvious secrets patterns.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should server be about speculative queuing (queue-for-retry)? Risk: speculative work costs CPU/GPU cycles. Need a credit model.
- How to express multi-tool prefetched dependencies (tool A likely calls tool B)? For now we scope to single-tool hints; multi-tool prefetch is future work.
- UX for long-running tool calls and streaming tokens: do we chunk speculative tokens vs committed result tokens?

Next actions / owners (first-pass):
- Product: finalize fallback policy editor UX (Maya) — 2024-11-20.
- Serving runtime: implement prefetch hint admission + metrics (Ethan) — spike by 2024-12-04.
- SDKs: design session.prefetch API surface and example widgets (Jonah) — PR by 2025-01-09.
- Security: review content scanning for prefetch hints (Samira) — 2024-11-25.

Notes to self (informal):
- keep prefetch tiny; we do not want to balloon session state retention.
- think about migrating to a later "active-warm" pool if the pattern proves highly valuable for select tools.
- mention to infra: will need light-weight per-session LRU for soft-warm handles; instrument ejection metric.

References:
- internal: CONFLUENCE-1234 (prefetch explorations), github PR 452 (stream framing prototype), JIRA-HOSTED-987 (circuit-breaker epic).
